question: Flat Rate vs. Free Shipping: What's the Difference?
metaDescription: Flat Rate charges a fixed (or calculated) cost every time; Free Shipping charges nothing, optionally requiring a coupon or minimum order amount.
shortAnswer: Flat Rate charges a defined cost for shipping within a zone — a single fixed amount, or one calculated from cart contents using its cost field's formula support — every time it's the selected method. Free Shipping charges nothing at all, and can be configured to always be available, require a specific coupon, or only appear once the cart reaches a minimum order amount.

bodyHtml:
How Each Method Works

Flat Rate's cost field accepts not just a plain number but a simple formula referencing cart totals, item counts, or per-item costs, letting it scale somewhat with order size while still being simpler to configure than full weight/dimension-based rating. Free Shipping's requirement setting controls exactly when it becomes available — always, only with a valid free-shipping coupon applied, only above a minimum spend, or a combination of coupon and minimum spend.

Common Configurations

  • Flat Rate as the default paid option, often alongside Free Shipping conditioned on a minimum spend, encouraging customers to add more to their cart to qualify.
  • Multiple Flat Rate instances within one zone (labeled "Standard" and "Express," for instance) giving customers a choice at different price points.
  • Free Shipping requiring a coupon as a promotional tool, rather than being a standing offer available to everyone.
  • Both methods can be enabled simultaneously within the same zone, letting WooCommerce display whichever ones currently qualify based on cart contents.

Choosing and Configuring These Methods

  1. Add Flat Rate for a straightforward, predictable shipping charge, using its formula field if costs should scale with the order.
  2. Add Free Shipping and configure its requirement (always, minimum spend, coupon) to match your promotional strategy.
  3. Combine both within a zone to offer a paid option alongside a free-shipping incentive.
